preamble: A palatalized alveolar stop [tʲ] shifting to the postalveolar affricate [tʃ]. In Upper Sorbian, Proto-Slavic *t before front vowels, palatalized in West Slavic (compare Polish ć [tɕ]), is written ć and pronounced [tʃ], merging with č.

examples.note: Soft t before a front vowel gave Upper Sorbian ć, pronounced [tʃ] (also infinitives in -ć, e.g. łhać /ˈfat͡ʃ/ 'to lie'). Whether an alveolo-palatal [tɕ] stage intervened is not shown in the sources.
